page: Amazon Web Services m7a.16xlarge is a general-purpose compute instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It is powered by a 64-core AMD EPYC 9R14 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The configuration allocates 64 physical cores mapped directly to 64 vCPUs with a single thread per core, avoiding hardware multithreading contention. Memory provisioning stands at 256 GB of DDR5 operating at 5 GHz, establishing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 4.0 GB per core. The instance provides 25 Gbps baseline network throughput. Hardware accelerators are absent with a zero GPU count, and local storage is listed as None, making network storage necessary for persistent file operations.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-threaded execution from the dedicated AMD EPYC core layout. The m7a.16xlarge achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core workloads, Geekbench multi-core processing, Clang software compilation, and ray tracing. Single-core benchmarks in stress-ng and Geekbench sit in the top 25%, supported by hardware instructions including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI. Memory subsystems record high throughput, demonstrating over 268 GB/sec in uncached read benchmarks and more than 8500 GB/sec in cached operations. The platform also yields top-tier performance in small model language prompt processing and medium model text generation, alongside strong Redis SET and relational database benchmark scores.

From an infrastructure perspective, the one-to-one mapping of physical cores to vCPUs provides predictable execution characteristics under sustained utilization. The absence of bundled local storage requires balancing network-attached block storage bandwidth against data ingestion requirements. Operating with high DDR5 memory throughput and broad vector instruction support, the instance delivers high compute density relative to standard general-purpose profiles. The m7a.16xlarge is technically appropriate for distributed caching clusters, large-scale CI/CD compilation workloads, backend web application fleets, and relational database management systems.
description: Amazon Web Services m7a.16xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and equipped with 64 dedicated x86_64 AMD EPYC 9R14 processor cores operating at 3.7 GHz. With a 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio, it supplies 256 GB of DDR5 system RAM clocked at 5 GHz, delivering 4.0 GB per core along with AVX-512 and AES vector instruction support. The instance includes 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, while omitting bundled local storage, necessitating external storage volumes for data persistence. Across benchmark evaluations, the m7a.16xlarge records top-tier multi-core execution in stress-ng, Clang compilation, and ray tracing, paired with strong memory bandwidth and Redis throughput. Because each vCPU corresponds directly to a physical core without multi-threading contention, the hardware configuration provides predictable resource density. This platform is technically suited for multi-threaded compilation pipelines, backend web serving fleets, in-memory caching layers, and high-concurrency database deployments.
